newsitem.title: PERU: Peru plans to spend 2.7 pct of 1997 GDP on debt.
newsitem.headline: Peru plans to spend 2.7 pct of 1997 GDP on debt.

text.p: Peru plans to spend 4.619 billion soles, or an estimated 2.7 percent of the country's gross domestic product, on debt service in 1997, according to the government's budget proposed to congress.

The budget proposal - obtained by Reuters - estimates an average exchange rate for 1997 of 2.70 soles to the dollar, which would mean the government will be making $1.710 billion in debt payments next year.

This would represent 18.7 percent of the 24.765 billion soles proposed budget. Monday, Economy and Finance Minister Jorge Camet said debt servicing next year would account for 18 percent of the budget.
The government's budget estimates the economy will grow five percent next year and be worth around 170 billion soles, according to President Alberto Fujimori.
The government has also proposed in its budget to take on a maximum $1.8 billion of new foreign debt next year.
Peru's total foreign debt was $32.445 billion at the end of March, according to the latest Central Reserve Bank of Peru figures.
